evidence:
WHAT IS SOUND. Dimension weights are the mandated policy: task/tests/scoring.toml:5-8 'functional = 0.6 / polish = 0.2 / visual = 0.2', byte-identical to the frozen template (sha256 95f70d6e... both) and score.py is byte-identical to the template (13de2b38...). Non-functional maximum contribution is 40% and score.py:47-48 zeroes the reward unless functional > 0.05, so style cannot be farmed without function. No dimension weight sits inside any [judge] block; no prompt or app_context restates a weight (grep). All 152 functional criteria are binary behaviours, none grades structure or style; polish's five binary criteria are behavioural (live update keeps entries, session resume, focus, refusal recovery, uncertain commit) rather than cosmetic; visual is five equal likert criteria (1.2 each). Family split inside functional (computed from the frozen judge.toml, sum of weights 64.404184): coordinated-change server contract 44 criteria = 28.9 (44.9%, 26.9 reward points), change-desk working behaviour 10 criteria = 15.5 (24.1%, 14.4 points), underlying offer desk 98 criteria = 20.004 (31.1%, 18.6 points). That split follows the brief's emphasis (instruction.md:1-3 headline, :5 'Keep the underlying offer desk working', :7-11 desk) and I do not fault it. The heaviest single rows (hro_change_lineage, hro_change_aba, hro_change_retry_concurrent, hro_change_overlap at 2.0; hro_desk_figures and hro_live_stale_mark at 2.5) are the defining behaviours.

DEFECT (per-criterion weights do not track what each thing proves). Inside the functional dimension, entry-retention and editing conveniences are weighted above the financial and access controls the product exists to enforce:
- functional/judge.toml:918 hro_change_over_budget weight = 0.5 (the only row that fails a coordinated commit that overruns a budget by a cent) versus :1368 hro_entries_reload = 1, :1377 hro_keep_revision_terms = 1, :1386 hro_keep_rescission_date = 1, :1314 hro_desk_remove_member = 1.5.
- All budget enforcement in the product: hro_change_over_budget 0.5 + hro_approval_budget 0.36170212 (:432) + hro_revision_budget 0.36170212 (:504) + hro_competing 0.4822695 (:630) = 1.7057 weight = 1.59 reward points out of 100. hro_change_net_budget (:909, 1.6) is passed by an app that performs no budget check at all, because it only requires affordable sets to commit.
- All anonymous-write protection: five ordinary rows at 0.1929078 (:766-801) + two coordinated rows at 0.18 (:1287, :1296) = 1.3245 weight = 1.23 points.
- The whole ordinary-desk access-control surface (12 anonymous rows, 4 forbidden-approver rows, 6 tier/band cells, hro_dual; 23 criteria) totals 4.0993 weight = 3.82 points, less than the four retention rows above (4.5 weight = 4.19 points).
- Same proof, different price: hro_restart (:900, whole-database durability across a real restart) 0.24113513 versus hro_change_retry_restart (:1125) 1; hro_competing (budget race) 0.4822695 versus hro_change_overlap 2; the four ordinary numeric-validation rows total 0.3617 versus hro_change_numeric 1.

SECONDARY OBSERVATIONS (not the basis of the Fail). (a) Three rows carry weight 0.01 (hro_req_create_recruiter :189, hro_referrer_roster :486, hro_draft_eligibility :648), i.e. 0.009 reward points each: effectively ungraded although counted as criteria; and sibling rows were shaved irregularly to fund them (hro_raise_role_recruiter 0.04889564 vs siblings 0.06889564; hro_concurrent_approval 0.06028368 and hro_stale_approval 0.05028368 vs revision/rescission siblings 0.09042553; hro_referral_creation 0.4722695 vs 0.4822695). (b) Because scoring.toml is fixed and functional has 152 criteria against 5 and 5, one visual likert is worth 4.0 points and hro_pol_focus 2.5 points while the largest functional criterion is 2.33 points; this is a consequence of template policy plus criterion count, not something this row can ask to change in scoring.toml. (c) 8.3 reward points sit on hro_pol_uncertain_commit and hro_keep_rescission_date, whose own text awards 0 when the judge's tooling cannot perform the interception; whether that is feasible is another row's question and is unmeasured.

MISSING MEASUREMENT. raw-evidence-index.json states 'Full configured grading/workload, reward discrimination/ranking and target/Oracle scores are absent.' The finding above is arithmetic on frozen bytes and source reading of criterion text; no configured judge run or mutated-app run has exercised it. No Oracle, model or portal score is claimed.
counterexample: Two submissions that are otherwise identical to a full-credit app. App X never refuses an over-budget settlement (ordinary approval, ordinary revision, competing approvals, coordinated commit) and accepts unauthenticated create/approve/revise/rescind and coordinated prepare/commit. It fails hro_change_over_budget, hro_approval_budget, hro_revision_budget, hro_competing, hro_anon_req_create, hro_anon_offer_create, hro_anon_approve, hro_anon_revise, hro_anon_rescind, hro_change_anon_prepare, hro_change_anon_commit = 3.0302 weight = 2.82 reward points lost. App Y enforces every budget and every sign-in check correctly but only the last change-desk member can be removed, the revision form resets after a refusal, and the rescission date is cleared after a failed request. It fails hro_desk_remove_member, hro_keep_revision_terms, hro_keep_rescission_date = 3.5 weight = 3.26 points lost. X, which lets anyone on the network settle money past the budget, outscores Y, which has three form inconveniences, by 0.44 reward points. (Conforming-alternative probe: I found no conforming app that a weight alone would fail; the defect is ordering, not a false fail.)
suggested_fix: In tests/scored/functional/judge.toml only (leave scoring.toml and score.py untouched), rebalance per-criterion weights so enforcement outweighs convenience: for example raise hro_change_over_budget to at least 1.5 and the budget, anonymous-write and restart rows of the ordinary desk to at least the weight of a retention row, lower hro_entries_reload, hro_keep_revision_terms, hro_keep_rescission_date and hro_desk_remove_member to about 0.5, and either give the three 0.01 rows a real weight or fold them into a sibling; then re-derive the family totals and re-run the mutated-app ordering check.
